featured.title: EB-2 India Just Went Dark. The July Bulletin Says 'Unavailable' — and Means It
featured.excerpt: For the first time this fiscal year, no EB-2 green cards will be issued to Indians at all. The number to watch now isn't a priority date. It's the calendar flipping to October.
featured.image_caption: A U.S. permanent resident (green) card; the July Visa Bulletin lists EB-2 India as unavailable
featured.nri_angle: EB-2 is the category most Indian H-1B professionals with advanced degrees are stuck in; its sudden 'Unavailable' status means no green card movement for them until at least October 2026.
featured.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: America Has Run Short of a Cancer Drug. It Just Sent an SOS to India's Drugmakers.
news.excerpt: The US FDA has quietly asked Indian manufacturers to supply ifosfamide — a chemotherapy in short supply after a US plant disruption — a reminder of how much the world's medicine cabinet leans on India.
news.image_caption: Vials of chemotherapy drugs; the US FDA has asked Indian manufacturers to help supply the cancer drug ifosfamide
news.nri_angle: An NRI family with a relative in cancer treatment in the US has a direct stake in whether ifosfamide stays on the shelf — and an Indian-made vial may be what fills the gap; the FDA's explicit appeal to Indian drugmakers underscores India's standing as the pharmacy of the world and offers the diaspora both reassurance and a recurring investment angle in names like Cipla, Alkem and Zydus.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: A Judge Killed Trump's $100,000 H-1B Fee. Two Weeks Later, It's Quietly Back.
news.excerpt: A Boston court struck down the fee on June 8 as an unlawful tax — then paused its own ruling. USCIS may keep collecting the six-figure charge while the appeal proceeds, and Indians, the largest H-1B group, are again left guessing.
news.image_caption: A US visa in a passport; a $100,000 fee on new H-1B petitions is back in effect while a federal appeal proceeds
news.nri_angle: Indians receive the largest share of H-1B visas, so the on-again, off-again fate of Trump's $100,000 fee — struck down on June 8 but back in force days later while the First Circuit weighs the government's appeal — directly governs whether Indian engineers, doctors and researchers can still realistically be sponsored, and the resulting uncertainty is pushing many toward Canada or a return to India.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: U.N. Halts Strait of Hormuz Evacuation After Cargo Ship Is Attacked, Stranding Thousands of Sailors Again
news.excerpt: A drone strike on a tanker off Oman forces the IMO to suspend a rescue that had just freed 1,100 seafarers, reviving fears for the fragile U.S.-Iran deal and the Indians who crew the world's ships.
news.image_caption: A tanker lies at anchor waiting to enter port. Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz had begun to recover before Thursday's attack forced the U.N. to pause its evacuation.
news.nri_angle: India is the world's largest supplier of merchant seafarers, with some 18,000 Indians caught on ships in the Gulf and three already killed; a renewed Hormuz crisis also raises India's oil-import bill and pump prices felt across diaspora families.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: America Will Soon Let You Pay $750 to Skip the Visa Line. India's Travellers Are the Obvious Customer.
news.excerpt: A six-month State Department pilot starting July 1 lets visitor-visa applicants buy an interview within 10 business days — a paid fast lane in a system where Indians have long waited months for a slot.
news.image_caption: The U.S. Embassy in New Delhi; a new State Department pilot offers Indian travellers faster visa interviews for a fee
news.nri_angle: Indians generate some of the world's heaviest demand for US visitor visas and have long faced months-long appointment backlogs, so a paid fast lane offering an interview within 10 business days — for USD 750 on top of the USD 185 fee — lands squarely on the diaspora's frequent fliers, from parents visiting grandchildren to founders and professionals shuttling across the India-US corridor.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: After a Decade of Waiting, India's Biggest Stock Exchange Is Finally Going Public. The Owner of the Market Is About to Join It.
news.excerpt: The National Stock Exchange has filed for a roughly Rs 30,000-crore offer-for-sale — set to be India's largest-ever IPO — at a valuation near $55 billion, ending a listing saga that has dragged since 2016.
news.image_caption: The National Stock Exchange building in Mumbai; NSE has filed for what would be India's largest-ever IPO
news.nri_angle: NRIs increasingly route remittances and savings into Indian equities and index funds, and the NSE IPO offers a chance to own a piece of the marketplace itself — a stock that has been off-limits until now — with eligible NRIs able to apply via NRE/NRO portfolio accounts, while the back-to-back NSE and Jio mega-listings signal the deepening of the very markets the diaspora uses to keep financial roots at home.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Adani Is Betting $2 Billion That the Next City Grows Around the Airport, Not the Other Way Around
news.excerpt: The group's airports arm will build 'airport cities' — hotels, offices, retail and entertainment — across more than 655 acres at six Indian airports, modelled on Singapore, Dubai and Amsterdam.
news.image_caption: An airport terminal in India; Adani Airports plans 'airport cities' across six Indian airports
news.nri_angle: NRIs experience India most often through its airports, and Adani's $2 billion bet on 'airport cities' at Mumbai, Ahmedabad and four other hubs means more hotels, business space and world-class terminals for diaspora travellers — while reshaping the earnings of a group that is a fixture of NRI investment portfolios directly and through Indian index funds.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: After Three Years of Talks, the India-UK Trade Deal Finally Goes Live July 15 — and It Quietly Rewrites the Rules for Indian Workers Abroad
news.excerpt: Cheaper Scotch and British cars grab the headlines, but the deal's real prize for the diaspora is a pact that spares some 75,000 Indian professionals from paying into two countries' social-security systems at once.
news.image_caption: India's commerce minister Piyush Goyal, in London for talks before the India-UK trade deal takes effect July 15
news.nri_angle: For Britain's 1.9-million-strong Indian community — the country's largest ethnic-minority group — the deal cuts tariffs that touch NRI-run import, restaurant and textile businesses, eases visas for chefs, yoga teachers and musicians, and, most importantly, ends the double social-security charge on the roughly 75,000 Indian professionals seconded to the UK who until now paid into two pension systems while collecting from one.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Twin Earthquakes Devastate Venezuela Near Caracas, Killing Scores — and the Shock Reaches India's Oil Bill
news.excerpt: Two powerful quakes struck barely 39 seconds apart, flattening buildings in a country already hollowed out by years of crisis, while a jump in crude prices ripples toward import-dependent India.
news.image_caption: Caracas, Venezuela; twin earthquakes near the capital have left thousands feared dead
news.nri_angle: A catastrophe in Venezuela reaches Indians on two fronts — the long-rooted Indian-origin communities across the Caribbean and Latin America with relatives and businesses in the region, and the wider economy at home, where a quake-driven rise in global crude prices lifts the import bill of a country that buys more than 85% of its oil abroad.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's Financial-Crime Agency Raided the World's Biggest Gold Processor. The Books Allegedly Didn't Match the Vault.
news.excerpt: After SEBI accused Rajesh Exports of inflating revenue by an almost unimaginable Rs 15.15 lakh crore, investigators found the physical gold was 40% short of what the ledgers claimed — and money trails running to the UAE and African mines that no one can fully account for.
news.image_caption: Refined gold bars; the ED found Rajesh Exports' physical gold stock about 40% short of its books
news.nri_angle: Through its Shubh Jewellers chain and the Valcambi refinery — a globally trusted source of minted gold bars and coins — Rajesh Exports sits close to the supply chain NRIs buy from for weddings, festivals and savings, so allegations that a marquee Indian gold name fabricated revenue on a record scale, routed metal through suspicious UAE channels and came up 40% short on physical stock strike directly at the diaspora's confidence in the integrity of Indian gold and in the Indian equities and jewellery brands many of them invest in.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: A Fire at a Tata Data Centre in Delhi May Have Erased 20 Years of One Company's Data. Google Cloud Was Hit Too.
news.excerpt: A June 5 blaze at the STT-Tata facility in Greater Kailash caused 'extensive damage,' and three weeks on the recovery is still failing — a warning about how much of digital India sits in a handful of buildings.
news.image_caption: Server racks inside a data centre; a June 5 fire at the STT-Tata facility in Delhi caused extensive damage
news.nri_angle: NRIs depend on Indian cloud and telecom infrastructure daily — from international SIMs and remittance apps to the e-governance portals used to renew OCI cards, file taxes and manage NRI accounts — so a Delhi data-centre fire that may have destroyed 20 years of one firm's records and disrupted Google Cloud across India is a direct warning about how concentrated, and how fragile, the digital systems holding diaspora documents and money can be.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Gold Just Broke Below $4,000 for the First Time Since November. It's Down a Quarter From Its Peak.
news.excerpt: A surging dollar, a Fed suddenly talking about rate hikes and fading Iran-war fears have wiped roughly 25% off gold since January — and India's own effort to defend the rupee by curbing gold imports is quietly part of the story.
news.image_caption: Gold bullion bars; spot gold fell below $4,000 an ounce for the first time since November 2025
news.nri_angle: Gold is the asset class woven into diaspora weddings, festivals and family savings, and NRIs are among the world's most active cross-border gold buyers — so a 25% crash from January's record reshapes their calculations at once: paper losses for recent buyers, a first real buying window before Diwali for those holding cash, and a stronger dollar that stretches remittances further in rupees even as the gold those rupees buy has cheapened.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Canada Has a Message for Indian Students: This Is the 'Best Time Ever' to Apply.
news.excerpt: As the US dangles visa expiry dates and Australia doubles its fees, Canada's envoy in Delhi insists the doors never closed — the student caps aren't even full, and Ottawa wants Indians to come.
news.image_caption: A Canadian university campus; Canada's envoy says it is the 'best time ever' for Indian students to apply
news.nri_angle: Study abroad is one of the largest financial and emotional decisions Indian families make and often the first foothold for a new branch of the diaspora; with the US, UK, Canada and Australia all tightening at once, an explicit invitation from Canada's envoy — caps unfilled and doors open — is significant for the lakhs of students choosing a destination, even as recent approval data and a warming India-Canada relationship counsel reading the welcome in full.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Amazon Just Doubled Down on India. It's Putting Another $13 Billion Into AI and the Cloud.
news.excerpt: The fresh commitment, announced Thursday, lifts Amazon's planned India spending to nearly $50 billion by 2030 — a vote of confidence in the country's data-centre boom that the diaspora's engineers and small businesses will feel directly.
news.image_caption: An Amazon Web Services data centre; AWS anchors Amazon's expanded AI and cloud investment in India
news.nri_angle: Amazon's additional $13 billion India investment — lifting its planned spend to nearly $50 billion by 2030 — deepens the country's AI and cloud capacity, creating senior technical roles at home that strengthen the case for diaspora reverse-migration, lowering costs for diaspora-founded startups that build on AWS, and promising affordable AI tools to millions of small Indian businesses with relatives abroad.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: America Has Run Out of EB-2 Green Cards for Indians This Year. The Wait Now Stretches to October.
news.excerpt: The State Department says the entire FY2026 allocation of employment-based second-preference visas for Indian applicants is gone — freezing one of the diaspora's main paths to a green card until the new fiscal year resets the count on October 1.
news.image_caption: The U.S. Department of State, which confirmed the EB-2 green-card category for India is exhausted for fiscal year 2026
news.nri_angle: The exhaustion of the EB-2 green-card category for India until October freezes one of the diaspora's main paths to U.S. permanent residency, stranding hundreds of thousands of Indian professionals — many long-time H-1B holders with families and homes — in temporary-visa limbo, and underscoring how the decades-old 7% per-country cap keeps Indian demand permanently mismatched with supply.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: An Indian-Origin Mayor Just Became the Most Powerful Kingmaker in Democratic Politics. All Three of His Picks Won.
news.excerpt: Zohran Mamdani, the son of filmmaker Mira Nair, watched his entire endorsed slate sweep New York's congressional primaries on Tuesday — ousting two sitting members of Congress and signalling that the city's first South Asian mayor now reaches far beyond City Hall.
news.image_caption: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, whose three endorsed candidates swept the city's Democratic congressional primaries
news.nri_angle: Zohran Mamdani — New York's first South Asian mayor and the son of filmmaker Mira Nair — has become a national Democratic kingmaker barely six months into office, showing that an Indian-origin politician can now sit at the centre of American power and reshape a major party, even as his democratic-socialist politics divide a diaspora that is no monolith.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Is Offering Its Scientists Abroad Up to Rs 60 Lakh a Year to Come Home. The Real Question Is Whether Money Is Enough.
news.excerpt: The Prime Minister Research Chair Scheme wants 120 Indian-origin researchers back from labs like OpenAI, DeepMind and Anthropic over five years, with grants of up to Rs 5 crore. Applications close July 15 — and the diaspora is doing the maths.
news.image_caption: India's IITs and IISc anchor the Prime Minister Research Chair Scheme 2026, which seeks to bring Indian-origin researchers home from global labs
news.nri_angle: The PMRC Scheme 2026 is India's most concrete and generous attempt yet to reverse its brain drain, offering Indian-origin researchers abroad up to Rs 60 lakh a year and Rs 5 crore grants to relocate to the IITs and IISc — putting a specific, deadline-bound offer in front of millions of diaspora scientists, even as the harder questions of lab quality and bureaucratic friction remain unanswered.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Washington Has a New Target in Its Immigration Crackdown: the Lawyers. The First Big Fine Involves Indian Asylum Claims.
news.excerpt: DHS says it has fined a single attorney more than $255,000 over 64 asylum documents filed mostly for Indian nationals — declarations it calls near-identical. For a community where word-of-mouth lawyers are how many navigate the system, the message lands close to home.
news.image_caption: U.S. immigration enforcement signage; DHS has begun fining attorneys over allegedly fraudulent asylum filings made largely for Indian nationals
news.nri_angle: Indians are among the fastest-growing groups seeking U.S. asylum, and DHS's new policy of fining the attorneys behind allegedly fraudulent claims means even genuine applicants tied to a flagged lawyer can see their cases reopened — making it essential for NRIs to verify a lawyer's license and never let anyone fabricate their persecution story.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: From Times Square to the Bund, the World Rolled Out Its Mat Again. India's Quietest Export Just Had Its Biggest Day.
news.excerpt: The 12th International Day of Yoga drew 35,000 to Kolkata's Red Road and millions across 2,500 venues in more than 210 Indian missions — a single morning in which the diaspora became, for a few hours, India's most visible ambassadors.
news.image_caption: Participants mark the International Day of Yoga, observed on June 21 across India and more than 2,500 venues worldwide
news.nri_angle: The International Day of Yoga is one of the few mornings each year when overseas Indians' own culture becomes the main public event in cities from New York to Toronto to Shanghai — a two-way act of belonging, organised by their consulates and open to everyone, that this year's 'Healthy Ageing' theme made quietly personal for a community thinking across continents and generations.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: The Diaspora's Money Is Pouring Home at Record Levels. It's Also Quietly Changing Shape.
nri-world.excerpt: India will take in nearly $140 billion in remittances this year. The bigger story is the shift from Gulf wages to Western capital — and how Delhi is racing to court it.
nri-world.nri_angle: For 18.5 million Indians abroad, sending money home is shifting from obligation to investment — and India is now pricing the bond with competitive interest rates, equity caps and property rule changes aimed squarely at the diaspora.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: A 23-Year-Old and His Mother Just Became Mayors a Week Apart. Both Still Teach Hindi on Weekends.
nri-world.excerpt: Tushar Kumar and Parveen Rani's back-to-back Hertfordshire mayoralties are a feel-good headline — and a window into how the diaspora's British political climb now runs through the council chamber.
nri-world.image_caption: A civic building in London, where Indian-origin councillors are steadily taking on mayoral and council roles
nri-world.nri_angle: Britain's 1.9-million-strong Indian community is building political power from the ground up — in town halls and civic chains — and the Kumar-Rani story captures the second-generation balancing act of staying rooted while serving a chosen country.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Every Summer, 10,000 Telugu-Americans Fill a Convention Center. It's Not Really About the Concert.
nri-world.excerpt: From TANA in Dallas to ATA in Baltimore, the diaspora's convention circuit has become the load-bearing infrastructure of a community trying to keep its language alive one generation at a time.
nri-world.image_caption: A Bharatanatyam dancer in traditional attire, the kind of classical performance that anchors diaspora cultural conventions
nri-world.nri_angle: The biennial Telugu conventions are an organised answer to the second-generation problem every immigrant community faces — how to pass on a language and culture that the home country can no longer enforce from 12,000 km away.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: India Has Quietly Rewritten the Rulebook for Its 4.5 Million OCI Holders. Here's What Changed.
nri-world.excerpt: A new digital e-OCI system, a USD 275 fee for fresh cards, a hard three-month deadline to update your record after a new passport, and the death of the old PIO card add up to the biggest shake-up of the scheme in years.
nri-world.image_caption: An Indian passport; India has overhauled the rules tying OCI cards to a holder's current passport
nri-world.nri_angle: The OCI card is the document that keeps roughly 4.5 million people of Indian origin connected to India — visa-free entry and the right to live and work there — and the 2026 overhaul raises fees, kills the old PIO card, and imposes a hard three-month deadline (with a penalty) to update the record after every new passport, hitting frequent flyers, overseas students and mixed-passport families hardest.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Forty-One Years On, the Diaspora Still Gathers for Air India 182. The State Mostly Doesn't.
nri-world.excerpt: On June 23, families lit candles from Stanley Park to Ahakista for the 329 people killed in the world's deadliest act of aviation terrorism before 9/11 — a grief that built Canada's South Asian community and a justice it never received.
nri-world.image_caption: The Air India Flight 182 memorial at Humber Bay Park East in Etobicoke, Toronto
nri-world.nri_angle: The 1985 Air India bombing killed 268 Canadians, most of them of Indian origin, and remains the deadliest terror attack in Canadian history — a foundational wound for the Indo-Canadian community, whose families have spent four decades organizing memorials and fighting the perception that their dead were treated as a foreign tragedy rather than a Canadian one.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Indian-Australians Give Generously. A New Study Wants to Know Why So Little of It Is Counted.
nri-world.excerpt: Now the largest overseas-born group in Australia, the community gives out of faith, family and duty — but mostly outside the formal channels that track, deduct and amplify philanthropy. Researchers think that is a missed opportunity worth measuring.
nri-world.image_caption: Performers play traditional drums at an Indian community cultural festival
nri-world.nri_angle: Indians are now the largest overseas-born community in Australia, yet their considerable charitable giving is largely invisible to the formal philanthropic sector because it flows through temples, family networks and remittances home rather than registered foundations — a gap a new research effort aims to map, with implications for how the diaspora's wealth shapes both Australian causes and India.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Europe Is Quietly Courting Indian Students — and Seeding the Diaspora's Next Chapter
nri-world.excerpt: The EU has awarded 75 Indians Erasmus Mundus scholarships and launched a student ambassadors' network, building the connective tissue that turns student flows into settled communities.
nri-world.image_caption: International students at a European university (Wikimedia Commons)
nri-world.nri_angle: Where students go is where communities eventually form. Europe's deliberate recruitment of Indian talent is the early signature of diaspora clusters that do not yet fully exist — as old America-or-Britain defaults loosen.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Prince William Just Gave Two Young Indians the Diana Award's Top Honour. Neither Lives Abroad.
nri-world.excerpt: An 18-year-old who built a power-cut-proof bulb and a 24-year-old mental-health campaigner were among 20 worldwide winners of the Diana Legacy Award, handed out in London.
nri-world.image_caption: Prince William, the Prince of Wales, who presented the Diana Legacy Awards in London
nri-world.nri_angle: For a community that prizes recognition abroad, two young Indians being honoured on a British stage by a future king — for solving Indian problems on the world's terms — is the diaspora's soft power at its purest.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: A Sunday Panel in Manhattan Showed What the Indian-American Community Actually Worries About Now
nri-world.excerpt: GOPIO's free 'College and Beyond' session put an AI engineer and a Hindi teacher on the same stage — a quiet bid to widen the diaspora's definition of a respectable career.
nri-world.image_caption: A community panel discussion; Indian-American leaders gathered in Manhattan to weigh the diaspora's current concerns (Wikimedia Commons)
nri-world.nri_angle: Volunteer-run community organisations are transmitting hard-won knowledge of the American higher-education maze to the diaspora's next generation — a sideways form of giving back that the CEO-and-Congress headlines miss.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Indian-Australians Mark 12th International Day of Yoga From Canberra to the Gold Coast
nri-world.excerpt: Diplomatic missions and community groups staged synchronised events nationwide, with this year's healthy-ageing theme resonating for a maturing diaspora.
nri-world.image_caption: Participants gather for an outdoor group yoga session marking International Day of Yoga.
nri-world.nri_angle: Shows how Australia's large and increasingly organised Indian community turned International Day of Yoga into a nationwide soft-power and community-building event.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: President Murmu Courts Indian Communities in Portugal and Slovakia on Europe Tour
nri-world.excerpt: A two-nation visit, including the first by an Indian head of state to Slovakia in 29 years, widens New Delhi's diaspora diplomacy across the EU.
nri-world.image_caption: President Droupadi Murmu, who toured Portugal and Slovakia to meet the Indian diaspora.
nri-world.nri_angle: Examines how India is extending its diaspora outreach to smaller European states, addressing the 125,000-strong Indian community in Portugal and a small but growing population in Slovakia.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: GOPIO Connecticut Marks 20 Years, Honours Five Leaders and Gives $50,000 to Charity
nri-world.excerpt: A two-decade-old diaspora chapter shows how Indian-American immigrant networks are maturing into permanent civic institutions.
nri-world.image_caption: A speaker addresses the GOPIO-CT 20th anniversary banquet in Darien, Connecticut.
nri-world.nri_angle: Chronicles how an Indian-American community organisation in Connecticut has evolved over 20 years into a durable civic institution, a model relevant to NRI communities across the United States.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: America Runs Short of a Cancer Drug — and Sends an SOS to India's Generic Makers
markets-finance.excerpt: With the chemotherapy drug ifosfamide in short supply, the US FDA has quietly asked Indian manufacturers to step in. The episode lifted pharma stocks and underscored, once again, the world's reliance on India's drug industry.
markets-finance.image_caption: The US FDA has asked Indian generic drugmakers to help supply the cancer drug ifosfamide amid a US shortage
markets-finance.nri_angle: It is a vivid reminder of how central India is to the medicines the diaspora and the wider world depend on — the same Indian generic makers being asked to rescue a US cancer-drug shortage are core holdings in many NRI portfolios, and the episode sits at the centre of the simmering India-US trade conversation.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Turns to Its Diaspora to Steady the Rupee — and Dangles an Unusually Sweet Deposit Deal
markets-finance.excerpt: By absorbing the cost of hedging, the Reserve Bank of India has let banks raise dollar-deposit rates to 6-7% for overseas Indians, with leverage potentially pushing returns far higher. Analysts see tens of billions in inflows.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India is absorbing hedging costs to draw diaspora dollar deposits and support the rupee
markets-finance.nri_angle: This is a scheme built expressly for the diaspora: it lets overseas Indians earn elevated, currency-risk-free returns on dollar deposits in Indian banks, turning the community's savings into both a personal opportunity and a national lifeline for the rupee — the most directly NRI-targeted financial move of the year.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Quietly Sells Down Its Crown Jewels — the IRFC Stake Sale Shows the Disinvestment Machine Is Back
markets-finance.excerpt: The government offloaded up to 2% of Indian Railway Finance Corporation at a discount, and institutions snapped it up. It is the latest in a string of stake sales as New Delhi leans on its state-owned giants to plug the budget.
markets-finance.image_caption: An Indian Railways train; the government sold up to 2% of Indian Railway Finance Corporation
markets-finance.nri_angle: These offer-for-sale windows in marquee state-owned companies are some of the most accessible entry points for NRIs to buy into India’s infrastructure and banking story, often at a built-in discount — so the return of an active disinvestment calendar directly shapes where diaspora investors can put their money to work back home.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Market Engine Has Quietly Switched Drivers — From Foreign Money to the Monthly SIP
markets-finance.excerpt: Even as foreign investors pulled roughly $36 billion out of Indian equities and the Nifty went almost nowhere for two years, ordinary savers kept feeding the market through automated monthly plans — a shift JP Morgan calls the country's new 'demand anchor.'
markets-finance.image_caption: Mumbai's financial district, where domestic monthly investment plans have become the dominant force in Indian equities
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRIs weighing whether to keep money in Indian equities should understand that the market is now propped up less by the foreign flows they watch in the headlines and more by a domestic savings wave — a structural change that affects both the risks and the resilience of any India allocation.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Is Quietly Talking Itself Out of Gold — and the World's Bullion Market Is Feeling It
markets-finance.excerpt: Domestic gold has slid to its lowest price since early April, dealers are quoting steep discounts, and the country's gold ETFs just logged their first monthly outflow in a year. Behind the cooling is a deliberate push to curb gold buying and defend a battered rupee.
markets-finance.image_caption: Indian gold demand has cooled to multi-month lows as the country curbs buying to defend the rupee
markets-finance.nri_angle: Gold is woven into diaspora life — the wedding jewellery, the festival purchases, the rupee-denominated savings that NRIs hold as a hedge — so India’s campaign to cool gold demand, the slide in domestic prices and the steep dealer discounts directly shape when and how non-resident Indians buy, gift and store the metal both abroad and back home.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Indian Markets Roar Back as Oil Crashes and the Central Bank Calms Rate Fears
markets-finance.excerpt: A day after a brutal selloff, the Sensex jumped nearly 800 points and the Nifty reclaimed 24,000, powered by banks and IT, as Brent crude tumbled to four-month lows on signs the Strait of Hormuz was reopening and the RBI signalled no rate hike is coming.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Sensex rallied nearly 800 points on June 24 as oil prices fell and the RBI eased rate-hike fears
markets-finance.nri_angle: The same falling oil price and steadier rupee that lifted Mumbai’s indices directly shape what NRIs see — the value of remittances sent home, the returns on Indian equity and bond holdings, and the cost of the fuel and imports that drive India’s inflation — and a fresh RBI rule now lets banks lend to non-resident Indians against their foreign-currency deposits.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Threw Open Its Bond Market to the World. The World Is Still Deciding Whether to Walk In.
markets-finance.excerpt: After scrapping the tax on foreign holdings of government bonds and widening access, India has lured early buyers — including a rare $1 billion bet by Canada's Fairfax — and is angling for a coveted Bloomberg index seat. But a weak rupee and steep hedging costs may yet keep the big money cautious.
markets-finance.image_caption: India's bond-market reforms aim to lure global investors as a weak rupee tests their appetite
markets-finance.nri_angle: India's push to pull global money into its government bonds runs on the same engine the diaspora is being courted with — dollar deposits, GIFT City, index inclusion — and the outcome will shape the yields, the rupee and the investment options NRIs see when they decide how much of their savings to send home.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Opens a New Door to the World's Markets — and It Runs Through GIFT City
markets-finance.excerpt: A wave of new funds is letting Indians invest in US stocks and global assets through the country's tax-neutral financial hub, with the fund itself shouldering the tax — but the fine print on remittance limits and levies still rewards a careful reading.
markets-finance.image_caption: An Indian financial-district skyline; new funds based in GIFT City are opening fresh routes for Indians and NRIs to invest in global markets
markets-finance.nri_angle: GIFT City is being built explicitly to court the diaspora's capital, and for NRIs weighing how to hold global assets with an Indian foot, the new IFSC funds change the calculus on tax, repatriation and paperwork — exactly the friction points that have long made cross-border investing a headache.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Jio Files for India's Biggest-Ever IPO — but This Time, the Marquee Backers Don't Get to Cash Out
markets-finance.excerpt: Reliance's digital arm has filed papers for a roughly $3.8 billion listing, with every rupee earmarked for debt and growth — meaning the Meta, Google and Gulf investors who poured in during 2020 will have to wait their turn.
markets-finance.image_caption: Reliance Jio's headquarters. Jio Platforms has filed a draft prospectus for what would be India's largest-ever IPO.
markets-finance.nri_angle: Jio's listing will be the marquee Indian IPO of a generation, and NRIs — long among the most eager retail buyers of marquee Indian names — will be weighing whether to chase it; the unusual all-fresh-issue structure and the holding-company discount are exactly the fine print diaspora investors need to read before committing.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Wants to Grow at 10%. First It Has to Explain Why Foreign Investment Has Dried Up.
markets-finance.excerpt: Net foreign direct investment fell to just $7.7 billion last year — a fraction of Vietnam's and Indonesia's — and India's top industry lobby says slow courts and five-year arbitration waits are scaring off the capital the country needs.
markets-finance.image_caption: India's financial capital, Mumbai, where weak foreign direct investment is testing the country's growth ambitions
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRIs are among the most natural foreign investors in India — through direct stakes, startups and property — yet the same slow courts and tangled dispute resolution that deter global capital are exactly what burn diaspora investors who get stuck in years-long litigation back home, making this a story about whether India can finally be trusted with their money.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Tata Motors Bets on a Five-Year Turnaround — ₹6 Lakh Crore in Revenue, and a Promise to Clear Its Debt
markets-finance.excerpt: At its investor day, Tata Motors' passenger-vehicle group set out targets to lift consolidated revenue past ₹6 lakh crore and reach a 10% margin by FY31, and to be net debt-free by FY29 — even as a cautious JLR outlook for FY27 left brokerages split.
markets-finance.image_caption: Tata Motors' Jaguar Land Rover unit, maker of the Range Rover, anchors the group's five-year turnaround plan
markets-finance.nri_angle: Tata Motors is both a heavyweight in the Nifty and Sensex that anchor most NRI India portfolios and the owner of Jaguar Land Rover, whose Range Rovers and Defenders the diaspora actually buys on the streets of London, New Jersey and Toronto — making its five-year bet a rare stock where the diaspora is invested in the shares and the showroom at once.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India’s Economy Just Cooled to a Three-Month Low — and a Resurgent Dollar Is Squeezing the Rupee Again
markets-finance.excerpt: Fresh data show India’s private-sector growth slowing and business confidence at its weakest in nearly four years, just as rising bets on a U.S. Federal Reserve rate hike push the dollar to a one-year high and drag the rupee and Indian stocks lower.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai; Indian markets pulled back as growth cooled and a stronger dollar pressured the rupee
markets-finance.nri_angle: For NRIs, the twin pressures matter directly: a weaker rupee stretches the value of dollars sent home or invested in India, while a cooling economy and a hawkish Fed reshape the calculus on when to remit, when to buy Indian equities, and how much currency risk to carry.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Big-League Cricket Has Moved Into the Oakland Coliseum — and the Bay Area's Team Lost the First Round
sports.excerpt: Major League Cricket's fourth season has turned the old A's ballpark into the home of the playoffs and the final, but the San Francisco Unicorns opened their Oakland stand with a 22-run defeat to the Texas Super Kings.
sports.image_caption: An aerial view of the Oakland Coliseum, which is hosting Major League Cricket matches, the playoffs and the 2026 final.
sports.nri_angle: Major League Cricket has brought top-flight T20 cricket — and its 2026 playoffs and final — to the Oakland Coliseum, putting international-calibre players within a short drive of the Bay Area's large South Asian diaspora.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Shafali Verma Drags India Out of the Danger Zone — and Into a Sunday Showdown With Australia
sports.excerpt: A 34-ball 53 anchored India's five-wicket chase of Bangladesh at Old Trafford, a must-win that keeps them second in a three-way logjam and sets up a final group decider against the unbeaten champions at Lord's.
sports.image_caption: Shafali Verma, whose 34-ball 53 anchored India's chase against Bangladesh at the Women's T20 World Cup.
sports.nri_angle: The Women's T20 World Cup is being played on English grounds, putting India's title defence within reach of diaspora fans across the UK — with Sunday's decisive group game against Australia at Lord's.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: A New Captain, and a 15-Year-Old Knocking: India Begin the Iyer Era in Belfast
sports.excerpt: Shreyas Iyer leads India for the first time in Friday's opening T20I against Ireland, and the toughest call of his debut is whether to break up a World Cup-winning top three to fit teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi.
sports.image_caption: Shreyas Iyer, who captains India in T20Is for the first time against Ireland in Belfast.
sports.nri_angle: The two-match series is played on diaspora doorsteps in the British Isles and offers NRIs a first look at India under new T20I captain Shreyas Iyer, plus the possible international debut of 15-year-old viral sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: One Centimetre, and the Record Is His Alone: Dev Meena Vaults to 5.46m
sports.excerpt: The 21-year-old from Madhya Pradesh cleared 5.46m at the National Inter-State Championships in Bhubaneswar, breaking the men's pole vault national record he had shared with his training partner and booking his ticket to the Asian Games.
sports.image_caption: Indian pole vaulter Dev Meena, who broke the men's national record with a clearance of 5.46m.
sports.nri_angle: Pole vault has rarely featured in NRI sports conversations, but Dev Meena's record run and dual Asian Games and Commonwealth Games qualification give diaspora fans a new Indian track-and-field name to follow as both Games approach.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: India's Women Won a Trophy and a Promotion in One Night in Auckland
sports.excerpt: Two first-quarter penalty corners beat hosts New Zealand 2-0 in the FIH Hockey Women's Nations Cup final, handing Salima Tete's unbeaten side the title and a direct return to the elite Pro League barely a year after relegation.
sports.image_caption: India captain Salima Tete, who led the team to an unbeaten FIH Hockey Women's Nations Cup title in Auckland.
sports.nri_angle: India's women returning to the FIH Pro League means diaspora fans across Europe and beyond will get far more chances to watch the national team play live next season, as Pro League fixtures tour host cities worldwide.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: India Have Never Won at Edgbaston. Now They Must — and Decide Whether to Risk Bumrah to Do It
sports.excerpt: Trailing England 0-1, Shubman Gill's young side arrives in Birmingham for the second Test on July 2 facing a green pitch, a venue that has beaten India eight times out of eight, and the recurring question of whether to spend their best bowler now or save him for Lord's.
sports.image_caption: India pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah, whose availability for the Edgbaston Test is the central selection question of the tour.
sports.nri_angle: Edgbaston sits in the heart of Britain's largest South Asian community, making the second Test the closest thing to a home game for UK-based Indian fans — a rare in-person chance to watch Shubman Gill's new-look side try to level the series and finally win at the one English ground that has always beaten India.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: India's 15-Year-Old Prodigy Will Change in a Room of His Own — the Safeguarding Rule Behind It
sports.excerpt: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi can sit in India's dressing room during play and join every team talk, but ICC and English safeguarding rules bar an under-16 from changing alongside adults — so on the tours of Ireland and England, his parents come too.
sports.image_caption: India's 15-year-old batting prodigy Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, named in the T20I squad for the tours of Ireland and England.
sports.nri_angle: Britain and Ireland's Indian community gets a rare home-soil look at India's 15-year-old prodigy this summer, and the UK safeguarding rules forcing a separate dressing room show how child-protection norms apply even to touring stars — with a potential record-breaking debut on local grounds.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Eighteen, and a National Record Twice in Forty Minutes: Anushka Yadav Announces Herself
sports.excerpt: On the opening night of the National Inter-State Championships in Bhubaneswar, an 18-year-old hammer thrower from a Baghpat village broke India's record twice — part of a record-laden evening that also sent Dev Meena and a returning Jyothi Yarraji to the Asian Games.
sports.image_caption: Bhubaneswar's Kalinga Stadium, host venue of the 65th National Inter-State Senior Athletics Championships, where multiple national records fell on the opening night.
sports.nri_angle: For a diaspora that follows Indian sport mostly through cricket, the Inter-State Championships show an Olympic-sport pipeline deepening — led by teenagers from farming and small-town families — ahead of the Asian Games in Japan this September, a stage the diaspora abroad can watch and rally behind beyond the cricket XI.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Neeraj Chopra Is Back — a Rusty Fourth in Doha, but a Glasgow Ticket in Hand
sports.excerpt: India's javelin great returned from a nine-month injury layoff at the Doha Diamond League, finishing fourth with 85.69m — enough to confirm his place at the Commonwealth Games, and a reminder that the comeback has only just begun.
sports.image_caption: Neeraj Chopra, India's first Olympic gold medallist in athletics, returned from a nine-month injury layoff at the Doha Diamond League.
sports.nri_angle: After the cricket team, Neeraj Chopra is the most recognised Indian athlete in the world and a fixture of NRI pride; his comeback opens a 2026 season — Commonwealth Games, European Diamond League legs, Asian Games — that runs through cities and time zones the diaspora can watch, and reach, from abroad.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Badminton's Biggest Stage Comes Home: India Hosts the World Championships for the First Time in 17 Years
sports.excerpt: Tickets are live for the BWF World Championships in New Delhi this August — and PV Sindhu, Lakshya Sen and Satwik–Chirag will play a Worlds on home soil for the first time in their careers.
sports.image_caption: India's PV Sindhu, the country's most decorated player at the BWF World Championships, headlines the home field in New Delhi this August.
sports.nri_angle: After cricket, badminton is the sport the Indian diaspora follows most closely — and PV Sindhu, Lakshya Sen and Satwik–Chirag are household names in NRI homes abroad. A home World Championships in mid-August, with global ticketing on BookMyShow, lands in the NRI summer-travel window and is exactly the kind of fixed-date event diaspora families plan an India trip around.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: India Finally Gave Its Track Stars a Night of Their Own — and Neeraj Chopra Owned It
sports.excerpt: At the inaugural Indian Athletics Awards in New Delhi, the Olympic javelin champion was named Best Male Athlete of 2025 — hours after flying in from his injury comeback in Doha — as India's federation set out to build a culture of recognition for the sport it now wins at beyond cricket.
sports.image_caption: Olympic javelin champion Neeraj Chopra, named Best Male Athlete of the Year 2025 at the inaugural Indian Athletics Awards in New Delhi.
sports.nri_angle: Neeraj Chopra is the rare Indian sporting icon who is not a cricketer — the most globally recognized face of India's Olympic ambitions and a unifying figure the diaspora follows from Tokyo to Paris. India's first-ever athletics awards night signals the country building institutions of recognition for track and field, the discipline diaspora children actually compete in at schools and colleges across the US, UK and Canada — and Chopra's message that Indians can match the world's best speaks directly to those kids.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: India Just Hosted Asia's Biggest Fencing Event for the First Time. Its Brightest Star Left With a Suspension.
sports.excerpt: The Asian Senior Fencing Championships came to New Delhi this week — a milestone for an Olympic sport India is only beginning to build — but a black card for Bhavani Devi, the country's first Olympic fencer, cast a shadow over the breakthrough.
sports.image_caption: Bhavani Devi, India's first Olympic fencer, in competition. A black card at the Asian Championships in New Delhi earned her a two-month suspension.
sports.nri_angle: Fencing is a European and East-Asian sport by tradition, but in the US, UK and Canada it is an established school and college sport and an Ivy League recruiting pathway — something many diaspora families know far better than relatives back home. India hosting the Asian Senior Fencing Championships for the first time, led by its one global star Bhavani Devi, is a bridge between the sport the diaspora lives with abroad and the country it came from.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Trump Called IBM's Indian-Born CEO a 'Legend.' Now He's Handed Arvind Krishna's Quantum Bet a Federal Tailwind.
technology.excerpt: Two new White House executive orders fast-track a working quantum computer by 2028 and post-quantum encryption by 2031 — and IBM, run by a Chennai-trained engineer, is the named beneficiary.
technology.image_caption: IBM chief executive Arvind Krishna speaking at SXSW in 2025
technology.nri_angle: An IIT Kanpur graduate now runs the company Washington is leaning on to win the quantum race — a milestone for Indian-American engineers and a signal to NRIs holding IBM stock or eyeing quantum careers.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Micron Just Told Wall Street the Memory Shortage Runs Past 2027. For the Diaspora, That's a Bill Coming Due.
technology.excerpt: Sanjay Mehrotra's company posted a blowout quarter and locked in $22 billion of advance customer commitments — but the same AI hunger that minted the gains is about to make laptops and phones pricier.
technology.image_caption: Micron Technology chief executive Sanjay Mehrotra
technology.nri_angle: An Indian-born CEO is riding the AI memory boom to record results, but the resulting chip shortage will quietly raise the cost of the laptops, phones and PC upgrades NRI families buy on both sides of the world.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: A $7 Billion Chip Deal Just Bet That AI's Next Battleground Isn't the Data Center. It's the Light Switch.
technology.excerpt: Onsemi's all-stock takeover of Synaptics pushes the chip industry toward 'physical AI' — and lands squarely on the edge-computing skills a generation of Indian engineers has been building.
technology.image_caption: Close-up of a semiconductor chip on a circuit board
technology.nri_angle: The pivot from cloud AI to 'edge' AI in everyday devices reshapes where chip jobs and skills will be valuable — a direct read for Indian engineers and NRI investors tracking the semiconductor sector beyond Nvidia.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: An Indian Air Force Pilot Just Became the First ISRO Astronaut on the Space Station. The Next Stop Is India's Own.
technology.excerpt: Shubhanshu Shukla's two weeks aboard the ISS are a dress rehearsal for Gaganyaan — and a recruiting poster for a space program the diaspora keeps funding from abroad.
technology.image_caption: Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla, the first ISRO astronaut to reach the International Space Station, in his Indian Air Force uniform.
technology.nri_angle: For an Indian family in New Jersey or the Bay Area, Shukla is the first of their own to fly to the space station — and the human face of a Gaganyaan program that diaspora engineers and donors have quietly been bankrolling.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: IndiaMART Connects 600 Buyers a Minute. Now It's Doubling Its AI Spend Every Six Months to Stop the Fakes.
technology.excerpt: India's biggest B2B marketplace is pouring money into AI to police counterfeit listings and replace call-centre work — a quiet test of whether Indian platforms can clean themselves up before regulators do it for them.
technology.image_caption: IndiaMART, India's largest B2B online marketplace, is doubling its AI spend to combat fraudulent listings (Wikimedia Commons)
technology.nri_angle: NRIs who source products from India for US storefronts — or who hold IndiaMART in their India portfolios — have a direct stake in whether the platform can scrub counterfeit and proxy sellers off a US 'Notorious Markets' watchlist.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: India Wants Its AI to Run on Indian Soil. A Navi Mumbai Company Is Stacking 80,000 GPUs to Make That Real.
technology.excerpt: Yotta's bet on 'sovereign' data centres — Blackwell chips, Indian data residency, no dependence on US hyperscalers — is the picks-and-shovels play behind India's AI ambitions. The diaspora's startups are the customers.
technology.image_caption: Rows of servers in a data centre; Yotta is stacking 80,000 GPUs to build sovereign AI infrastructure in Navi Mumbai
technology.nri_angle: Indian AI startups founded by returnees and NRIs need compute that keeps data inside India for regulatory and cost reasons — Yotta's GPU farms are the rails those companies, and diaspora investors backing them, are betting on.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Microsoft Bankrolled the AI Giants. Now Satya Nadella Is Picking a Fight With Them.
technology.excerpt: The Hyderabad-born CEO warns AI can't 'hollow out' white-collar work — the work his own Indian engineers do most — while a model-agnostic Copilot quietly reshapes the race.
technology.image_caption: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, who has called for an AI 'reset' away from a few dominant model makers.
technology.nri_angle: Nadella's warning against AI 'hollowing out' white-collar jobs lands directly on the young Indian engineers — in Hyderabad, Bengaluru and on H-1B visas in the US — whose entry-level coding roles are most exposed, and a commodity-AI world gives India's services giants room to survive.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Everyone's Chasing AI Chips. An Indian-American Duo Just Raised $190 Million Building the Wires Between Them.
technology.excerpt: Upscale AI hit a $2 billion valuation with Nvidia and Azim Premji's fund backing it — and its founders' résumés read like a tour of Silicon Valley's Indian engineering diaspora.
technology.image_caption: High-speed networking between AI servers — the bottleneck Upscale AI's silicon targets, backed by a 90 million raise
technology.nri_angle: While layoff headlines hit Indian software engineers, the AI infrastructure layer — led by diaspora veterans like Upscale's Barun Kar and Rajiv Khemani and Arista's Jayshree Ullal — is hiring and offers NRI engineers and investors a more defensible bet than the model labs.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: The Firm That Spotted Zomato Early Just Put Half Its Money Into AI and Deeptech
technology.excerpt: Info Edge has quietly poured ₹1,003 crore into 54 AI and deeptech startups — and for NRI investors it's a rare public-market window into India's next tech decade.
technology.image_caption: Info Edge, the Naukri.com parent that backed Zomato early, is putting half its investments into AI and deeptech (Wikimedia Commons)
technology.nri_angle: Info Edge is among the most-watched listed proxies for India's startup economy, giving NRI investors early, diversified exposure to AI and deeptech they otherwise can't reach — and the ventures it funds are exactly the kind that make a return-to-India career move credible.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: India Won't Ban Crypto. It Just Made Sure It Can See Every Trade Over $10,000.
technology.excerpt: A new reporting order for over-the-counter deals, plus fresh Travel Rule pop-ups on Binance, signal the government's real crypto policy: tolerate it, tax it, and trace it.
technology.image_caption: Cryptocurrency; India will monitor large crypto trades rather than ban them
technology.nri_angle: NRIs who move money between Indian and US wallets, or hold Indian-exchange accounts from abroad, now face name-and-PAN disclosure on transfers — a compliance headache that turns cross-border crypto into a paper trail.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Qualcomm Spent 25 Years Selling Phone Chips. It Just Told Wall Street Two-Thirds of Its Future Isn't Phones.
technology.excerpt: An Investor Day blitz — a $40 billion non-handset target, Meta and Microsoft as data-center customers, and a $3.9 billion software buy — repositions the company as an AI infrastructure player. The talent it needs is heavily Indian.
technology.image_caption: Qualcomm; the chipmaker says most of its future revenue will come from outside smartphones
technology.nri_angle: Qualcomm's pivot into AI data-center chips is a hiring story as much as a strategy story — it opens a new front in the Silicon Valley engineering job market just as legacy IT firms shed roles, and Indian chip-design talent sits at the center of it.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Anthropic and Amazon Just Picked 40 Indian Startups to Build the Next Wave of AI Agents. The Catch: No Equity, Big Strings.
technology.excerpt: An India-first accelerator hands early-stage founders Claude access and $70,000 in credits. It is also a quiet land-grab for the developer loyalty that will decide who owns India's AI stack.
technology.image_caption: A tech park in Bengaluru; Anthropic and AWS selected 40 Indian startups to build agentic-AI products
technology.nri_angle: For NRI founders and angel investors, this is the clearest signal yet that the agentic-AI startup action is moving to Bengaluru — and that US frontier labs, not just US capital, now compete directly for India's best builders.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Zendaya Walked the Paris Spider-Man Carpet in a $35 eBay T-Shirt — and Broke the Internet Doing It
entertainment.excerpt: No gown. No couture. Just a vintage Spidey tee styled as a minidress and a pair of white Louboutins — and somehow it became the most talked-about red carpet look of the week.

entertainment.title: Salman Khan Is Reportedly Becoming Karna — and Bollywood Just Got Its Most Ambitious Epic in Years
entertainment.excerpt: After years of mass-action romps, Bhai is in advanced talks to play the Mahabharata's most tragic warrior in a two-part epic directed by Rakeysh Omprakash Mehra and backed by Farhan Akhtar's Excel Entertainment. The body transformation alone tells you how serious this is.

entertainment.excerpt: Milly Alcock and Jason Momoa's DC outing opens in India on June 26 — but the version playing in Mumbai isn't the one playing in Manhattan. After 'Superman' lost its kiss last year, the censor board is back, and NRIs are once again watching the uncut cut from their couches.

entertainment.title: Ten Years After Kattappa Killed Baahubali, Netflix Opens the Gates of Mahishmati Again — This Time There's No Script
entertainment.excerpt: 'Baahubali: The Torchbearer' lands worldwide on June 26 — the docu-series that finally lets you behind the curtain of the film that taught Indian cinema to dream in IMAX.
entertainment.image_caption: Prabhas, who plays Amarendra and Mahendra Baahubali in S. S. Rajamouli's franchise (Wikimedia Commons)

entertainment.title: Riteish Deshmukh Spent Ten Years Becoming a King. This Friday, 'Raja Shivaji' Storms Netflix Worldwide.
entertainment.excerpt: The Marathi epic that became only the second film in its language to cross ₹100 crore lands on Netflix on June 26 — and yes, Salman Khan's sword-swinging cameo travels with it.

entertainment.excerpt: Milap Zaveri's monsoon romance just moved up a week, dropped its full title track, and quietly became one of the summer's most-watched debuts — for reasons that have everything to do with a famous surname.

entertainment.title: Shraddha Kapoor Gives Birth Backstage, Then Walks Out to Dance: The 'Eetha' Teaser Is a Knockout
entertainment.excerpt: She's never gone this raw. As a legendary Lavani queen who refuses to leave the stage even mid-labour, Shraddha Kapoor delivers the line — and the look — that has Bollywood whispering 'National Award' before a single full scene has dropped.
entertainment.image_caption: Shraddha Kapoor, who plays Lavani legend Vithabai Narayangaonkar in Eetha (Wikimedia Commons)

entertainment.title: King Khan Picks Christmas — and Walks Straight Into a Hollywood Ambush With Avengers, Dune and The Rock
entertainment.excerpt: Shah Rukh Khan and Siddharth Anand have locked December 24 for their Pathaan reunion. The catch: Doomsday, Dune 3 and Jumanji are all crashing the same holiday week.
entertainment.image_caption: Official poster for King, starring Shah Rukh Khan (Wikipedia)
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: "His Mother? Are You Mad?" Mouni Roy Heard the Whole Internet Laugh — and Decided She Didn't Care
entertainment.excerpt: The Naagin star is exactly one year older than Varun Dhawan. She plays his fake mother in David Dhawan's latest. And her answer to the trolls is the most relaxed thing she's ever said.
entertainment.image_caption: Mouni Roy, who plays a fake mother to Varun Dhawan in Hai Jawani Toh Ishq Hona Hai (Wikimedia Commons)

entertainment.title: Ranveer Singh Picked Up the Phone Himself. Now South Cinema's Quiet Star Is Walking Into a Zombie Apocalypse — and Bollywood.

entertainment.excerpt: On his late father Veeru Devgan's birth anniversary, the OG action star announced 'Chauhaan' — a Kashmir-set mass actioner landing October 1, 2027 — and the internet immediately decided which Khan he was throwing shade at.

entertainment.title: TVF Stopped Apologizing for Not Being 'Panchayat.' 'Gram Chikitsalay' Season 2 Finally Found Its Own Heartbeat — in a Crumbling Village Clinic.
entertainment.excerpt: Amol Parashar's earnest Dr. Prabhat returns to Bhatkandi on Prime Video, and this time the rural dramedy walks out of Phulera's shadow — with a Bhojpuri superstar, a fake doctor who Googles his prescriptions, and a 'will-they-won't-they' the writers swear even they can't call.

lifestyle-health.title: A Single Habit — Regular Exercise — May Head Off Nearly Half of Dementia Cases, Researchers Say
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Of the fourteen lifestyle and environmental factors that shape dementia risk, six can be tackled through exercise alone, University of Minnesota researchers report — and a virtual program shows even rural adults far from gyms can do it from home.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Researchers say regular exercise can address six of the fourteen modifiable risk factors for dementia
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians carry an elevated, earlier risk of both diabetes and dementia, and aging diaspora parents are often scattered far from family and specialist care — so a finding that one accessible, no-cost habit, deliverable even by telehealth at home, can address six of dementia's biggest risk factors is unusually relevant to Indian-origin households.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Three Everyday Sleep Habits May Be Quietly Aging the Brain, a 23,000-Person Study Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Sleeping outside the recommended seven-to-nine-hour window, napping often during the day and struggling with sleeplessness were each linked to more of the brain damage that builds up with age — and all three, researchers note, can be changed.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A study of 23,000 middle-aged and older adults links three common sleep habits to brain aging
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Indian-origin professionals abroad routinely run on short, broken sleep — late video calls with family in India, demanding jobs across time zones, the cultural habit of the afternoon nap — so evidence that these specific patterns may accelerate brain aging hands the diaspora a concrete, no-cost lever to protect long-term cognitive health.

lifestyle-health.title: Even 'Safe' Air May Be Hardening the Heart's Arteries, a Large Imaging Study Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Scanning the hearts of more than 11,000 adults, researchers found that long-term exposure to air pollution — even at levels below regulatory limits — was tied to more advanced coronary artery disease, with women facing a markedly higher risk.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A large imaging study tied long-term air pollution, even at safe levels, to more advanced coronary artery disease
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Indian-origin families straddle two air-quality worlds — long stays in some of the planet's most polluted cities back home and daily life in Western suburbs assumed to be clean — so a finding that even 'safe' air damages arteries reframes pollution as a heart risk the diaspora carries in both places, on top of an already high genetic burden of cardiovascular disease.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: It May Not Be How Much You Move, but How Many Ways — Exercise Variety Is Linked to a Longer Life
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A large analysis finds that people who mix walking, lifting, cycling and other activities have lower death rates than those who rely on a single form of exercise — even after accounting for how much they do in total.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A new analysis links variety in physical activity, not just total volume, to lower mortality
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Many in the Indian diaspora settle into one fitness rut — the daily treadmill walk, the weekend cricket match, the gym routine that never changes — so evidence that mixing activity types adds years, independent of how much you do, offers a practical, low-cost upgrade for busy NRI households trying to outrun the community’s high cardiometabolic risk.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Plant-Forward Mediterranean Diet Was Tied to a 26% Lower Heart-Disease Risk Over 20 Years, a Study Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Following more than 3,000 Greek adults for two decades, researchers found that those who ate the most vegetables, fruit, legumes, grains and fish had dramatically lower cardiovascular risk — while calorie-heavy diets light on lean meat fared worst.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A plant-forward Mediterranean diet of vegetables, legumes, grains and fish was tied to lower 20-year heart-disease risk
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: A plant-forward pattern built on vegetables, legumes, whole grains and fish maps closely onto traditional Indian vegetarian and coastal cooking — so for a diaspora whose diets have drifted toward calorie-dense, processed convenience food abroad, this 20-year evidence is a reminder that the heart-protective template may already sit in their own kitchens.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: It Isn't Being Alone That Ages the Mind — It's Feeling Lonely, a 175,000-Person Study Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Drawing on data from 18 countries, researchers found that the perception of loneliness, far more than simply living a solitary life, predicted faster cognitive decline and a shorter life — a distinction with real consequences for how families care for ageing parents.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A 175,000-person study across 18 countries found feeling lonely, more than living alone, tracks with faster cognitive decline (Openverse)
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: For Indian families spread across continents — children in the US or UK, parents back home — this study reframes the worry: a grandparent who lives alone but feels connected may fare far better than one surrounded by people yet quietly lonely, a nuance that should reshape how the diaspora thinks about long-distance caregiving.

lifestyle-health.title: Cholesterol Pills May Touch More Than the Heart — a Genetic Study Maps Effects on Weight, Hormones and the Brain
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Using DNA rather than years of follow-up, Australian researchers found that statins and the newer PCSK9 inhibitors carry distinct side-effect signatures — from body fat and testosterone to lung function and even brain size — a reminder that two drugs aimed at the same target are not interchangeable.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A genetic study finds statins and PCSK9 inhibitors carry distinct effects beyond cholesterol, from weight and hormones to lung and brain
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians carry one of the world's highest burdens of early heart disease, and statins are a fixture in many NRI households; this study is a nudge to treat cholesterol medication as a personalised decision — worth a real conversation with a doctor — rather than a one-size-fits-all pill.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Poor Sleep in the Teenage Years Casts a Long Shadow Into Adulthood, a New Study Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Tracking young people from age 15 to 22, researchers found that irregular sleep and insomnia symptoms as a teenager predicted worse health, more hospital stays and lower life satisfaction years later — evidence that adolescent sleep is an investment, not a luxury.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Researchers tracked young people from age 15 to 22, linking poor teenage sleep to worse adult health
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: In high-achieving Indian and South Asian households, late-night study, packed extracurriculars and the quiet glorification of running on little sleep are common among teenagers chasing top grades and college admissions — so evidence that adolescent sleep shapes health and wellbeing for years afterward speaks directly to how diaspora families weigh academic pressure against rest.

lifestyle-health.title: Cutting Out Sugar Entirely May Backfire, a New Study Warns — Balance Beats Elimination
lifestyle-health.excerpt: In a 16-week experiment, animals fed a low-fat diet stripped of all table sugar developed gut imbalance, insulin resistance and early fatty-liver changes — even though they gained no extra weight. The lesson, researchers say, is that the body needs balanced carbohydrates, not a zero.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A 16-week study found that a low-fat diet with all table sugar removed harmed gut and metabolic health in mice
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Sugar has become the villain of choice in diaspora wellness circles — 'no-sugar' challenges, sugar-free mithai and zero-sugar swaps are everywhere among health-conscious NRIs guarding against the community’s steep diabetes risk — so a study suggesting that total elimination can harm gut and metabolic health is a timely reminder that balance, not a blanket ban, is what protects the body.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: For Yo-Yo Dieters, the Trick May Be When You Eat, Not How Much You Count
lifestyle-health.excerpt: An 18-month Australian trial found intermittent fasting matched old-fashioned calorie counting for weight loss — but felt far easier, because dieters never had to police every mouthful. About a sixth of their success came down to that lighter mental load alone.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: An 18-month Australian trial found intermittent fasting matched calorie counting for weight loss but felt easier to sustain
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: In Indian and South Asian homes food is love, hospitality and ritual — the calorie-counting diet, with its weighing of every roti and ladoo, collides head-on with that culture, which is exactly why a fasting approach the community already knows from vrat and Ekadashi may prove far easier to live with.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Strict Low-Carb Diet Eased Hard-to-Treat Depression in a New Trial — but Doctors Urge Caution
lifestyle-health.excerpt: In a UK study of people whose depression had resisted standard treatment, six weeks on a ketogenic diet brought a slightly bigger drop in symptoms than a healthy comparison diet — a tantalising hint that what we eat may reach the brain, not just the body.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A UK trial tested a strict ketogenic diet against a healthy comparison diet in people with treatment-resistant depression
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Depression remains heavily stigmatised in many Indian and South Asian families, where it is often hidden or dismissed rather than treated — so any evidence that a dietary change, framed as wellness rather than illness, can ease symptoms may reach people who would never walk into a psychiatrist’s office.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Three Years of Diet and Exercise Paid Off for Two Decades — Far Beyond Diabetes, a New Study Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: People with prediabetes who followed an intensive diet-and-exercise program were 21% less likely to pile up multiple chronic diseases over the next 20-plus years — and the protection held even after diabetes itself was taken out of the equation.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A new study finds a few years of diet and exercise can cut chronic-disease risk for decades (Wikimedia Commons)
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians slide from prediabetes to diabetes faster and younger than most populations, and rarely stop there — heart disease, kidney trouble and more tend to stack up; this study shows a few years of disciplined diet and movement at the prediabetes stage can blunt that whole cascade decades later, not just the diabetes.
